implementation_notes: In the Swift server ecosystem the transport comes from the framework: with Vapor the route helper is the entire route structure - app.get("healthz") { req in ... } returns anything ResponseEncodable - and a SwiftNIO-based service answers the same path inside its channel pipeline. What remains is the check set as ordinary Swift code under a deadline (ideally an async closure) and the split between liveness and readiness, for which Swift has no standard library: keep it as a small type the route consults, or accept a plain liveness route plus a readiness route that checks the instance-local resources. Before writing one, check whether the platform's existing HTTP probe on a real route is already a faithful signal.
idiom_name: Vapor route handler app.get("healthz") (or a SwiftNIO responder)
pitfalls: Route handlers run on SwiftNIO event loops: a blocking check (synchronous database call, file I/O, lock) blocks the loop and stalls both the probe and the traffic it is meant to protect.
A route registered inside a group with authentication or session middleware cannot be answered by an orchestrator - register the health routes outside the protected group explicitly.
Errors thrown inside a handler are converted by the framework's error middleware (typically 500) rather than by your status mapping; catch dependency failures and return the intended status code.
